goal: Find your Mac's name and network address

steps.title: Open System Settings
steps.explanation: Click the Apple menu in the top left corner, then choose System Settings.

steps.title: Open General settings
steps.explanation: In the left sidebar, click General. You may need to scroll down to find it.

steps.title: Open About
steps.explanation: Click About to see your computer's details.

steps.title: Read your computer's name
steps.explanation: Your computer's name is shown to the right of the Name field. Others on your network can find your Mac by this name.

steps.title: Open Sharing settings
steps.explanation: Go back to General in the sidebar, then click Sharing to find your local network name.

steps.title: Read your local network name
steps.explanation: Look at the bottom of the window. This is your computer's name with .local added, and spaces replaced with hyphens. For example, My Computer becomes My-Computer.local.

steps.title: Open a sharing service that's on
steps.explanation: In the Sharing window, click to the right of a service that is turned on, such as Screen Sharing or File Sharing.

steps.title: Read your network address
steps.explanation: The network address for that service appears in the window. It looks something like vnc://10.212.167.33 or smb://name.example.com. Only share it with people you trust.
